experiment: C1 confirmatory synthetic concept cohort v3 scenario anchors
purpose: Freeze generic scenario and intent constraints for a full-batch v3 regeneration without freezing final request wording.

generation_contract.pair_style_rule: For every reciprocal pair, both concepts use the same ordered discourse slots and split assignments; content must remain concept-specific.

discourse_slots.instruction: Present one observed phenomenon and request its causal mechanism.
Contrast two conditions and request an explanation of the difference.
Pose a prospective design decision and request relevant tradeoffs or safeguards.
Describe a concrete failure pattern and request a mechanism-focused diagnosis.
Introduce a new setting and request a prediction under one changed condition.
Provide a generic observation pattern and request interpretation of the underlying mechanism.

train.scenario_anchor: A long-running graph workspace retains cycles of task objects after every external root to those tasks disappears; request an explanation of root tracing, reachability, cycle handling, and safe reclamation.

Short-lived request objects disappear quickly while a smaller set of objects survives through many processing rounds; contrast how generational collection treats young and repeatedly surviving objects without discussing allocator placement.

An interactive simulation must reclaim unreachable objects while keeping response pauses small; ask about concurrent or incremental tracing tradeoffs among pause time, throughput, and collector coordination.

An extension registry accidentally keeps references to otherwise obsolete objects, so memory remains occupied indefinitely; diagnose why still-reachable objects cannot be collected and how roots or reference lifetimes cause the leak.

test.scenario_anchor: A scene graph changes from gradual object retirement to large bursts in which entire disconnected subgraphs lose their roots; predict how tracing workload, reclamation timing, and pause behavior change under bursty unreachability.

Runtime logs show frequent young-object collections, repeated survivor promotion, and occasional longer full-heap scans; interpret the pattern in terms of generations, survival, roots, and full tracing.

train.scenario_anchor: A buffer manager has enough total free bytes but cannot satisfy a request for one large contiguous block; request an explanation of external fragmentation, free-block layout, splitting, and coalescing.

One workload requests nearly uniform blocks while another alternates many small requests with occasional large ones; contrast internal waste, external fragmentation, and allocation latency across the two size patterns.

A real-time service needs a free-list policy for variable-size blocks under a strict latency budget; ask about placement, splitting, search cost, and fragmentation tradeoffs without invoking object reachability.
An allocator leaves adjacent released blocks separate, and large requests begin failing after prolonged churn; diagnose missing coalescing and the resulting distribution of unusable free regions.

test.scenario_anchor: A device changes its alignment requirement so every requested block must begin on a wider boundary; predict how padding, internal fragmentation, and effective capacity change.

Telemetry shows rising allocation latency, many tiny free regions, and stable total free capacity; interpret the evidence as a placement and fragmentation problem and identify useful allocator statistics.

train.scenario_anchor: A remote actuator must accept commands only from an authorized controller and reject captured commands replayed later; request how keyed authentication, identity binding, nonces, and freshness establish origin and replay resistance.

One message system has a single verifier sharing a secret, while another must let many independent verifiers check the sender; contrast message authentication codes and digital signatures in trust, key distribution, and verification.

An intermittently connected terminal must verify credentials without accepting stale challenge responses; ask about challenge-response design, credential handling, freshness state, and recovery tradeoffs.

A correctly signed transaction is accepted twice because the verifier never records or checks request freshness; diagnose why signature validity alone does not stop replay and how freshness checks repair the protocol.

test.scenario_anchor: A credential system rotates its signing key while some verifiers temporarily retain only the previous verification key; predict authentication failures and security risks during a staged key transition.
Audit records show valid authentication tags on duplicated requests that reuse an earlier nonce; interpret the evidence as a freshness or replay-state failure rather than accidental corruption.

train.scenario_anchor: A sensor link experiences accidental bit flips during transmission and appends a small check value to each packet; request how parity or checksums reveal accidental changes without making any identity or anti-forgery claim.

One noisy channel produces isolated bit flips while another produces short bursts of adjacent errors; contrast how code distance and cyclic redundancy structure affect detection of the two error patterns.
A storage controller must choose the length and complexity of a check value for fixed-size data blocks; ask about overhead, computation, and accidental-error detection tradeoffs only.
A simple checksum fails to flag a recurring accidental byte-reordering pattern; diagnose the checksum weakness and explain why a more structured error-detecting code may cover that pattern.

test.scenario_anchor: The payload size grows substantially while the appended accidental-error check remains the same length; predict how the chance of undetected random corruption and the protection-overhead ratio change.

Controlled noise tests report detection rates for single-bit, double-bit, and burst errors under several check polynomials; interpret which structural properties of the codes explain the observed accidental-error coverage.

train.scenario_anchor: A brief heat stress causes newly made proteins to expose hydrophobic regions and begin aggregating; request how chaperones, refolding attempts, ubiquitin tagging, and proteasomal disposal protect the cell.

A stable protein remains soluble while a sequence variant of the same protein repeatedly misfolds under identical conditions; contrast folding stability, chaperone engagement, degradation, and aggregation outcomes.

A cell culture faces oxidative damage to existing proteins rather than a surge in protein synthesis; ask how refolding capacity and selective degradation could be supported without preserving irreparable proteins.

Ubiquitin-tagged proteins accumulate after proteasomal throughput declines, even though chaperone activity remains intact; diagnose the disposal bottleneck and its consequences for aggregation and stress responses.

test.scenario_anchor: A long-lived structural protein becomes chemically damaged while the available pool of folding chaperones is reduced; predict how triage between refolding, tagging, degradation, and aggregation changes.

A pulse-tracking experiment shows decreasing refolded protein, increasing tagged protein, and delayed aggregate formation; interpret which quality-control stage is limiting and why the aggregate signal appears later.

train.scenario_anchor: A newly synthesized surface receptor remains in an internal compartment instead of reaching the plasma membrane; request the causal sequence of cargo sorting, vesicle budding, targeting, and membrane fusion.

Two internalized receptors enter the same early compartment, but one returns to the surface while the other proceeds toward degradation; contrast endosomal sorting, recycling signals, and routing to later compartments.

An artificial membrane carrier must deliver a generic cargo to one intracellular compartment while avoiding off-target fusion; ask about targeting cues, uptake, membrane composition, fusion specificity, and delivery tradeoffs.
Cargo-filled vesicles accumulate beside the correct target membrane after a tethering or fusion factor is lost; diagnose which trafficking step failed and why cargo sorting alone is insufficient.

test.scenario_anchor: A surface receptor changes from rapid recycling to entry into a pathway that reaches a degradative compartment; predict changes in surface abundance and the sequence of vesicle-routing events.

Time-lapse imaging shows cargo leaving a donor compartment, pausing in small carriers, and accumulating before one target membrane; interpret whether budding, transport, tethering, or fusion is the likely limiting step.

train.scenario_anchor: A bacterial community begins producing a shared surface matrix only after cell density passes a sharp threshold; request how secreted signal accumulation changes transcription and coordinates matrix production.
Communities with the same cell count coordinate in a closed chamber but not under rapid fluid flow; contrast signal retention and washout while keeping nutrient exchange outside the explanation.
A treatment process aims to delay harmful biofilm formation by degrading extracellular communication signals; ask about threshold shifting, incomplete suppression, dispersal, and selection tradeoffs.

A strain that cannot synthesize its usual signal fails to activate a coordinated extracellular-enzyme program at high density; diagnose the signaling failure and distinguish signal production from signal response.

test.scenario_anchor: The same number of cells is divided among much smaller sealed droplets instead of one large vessel; predict how local signal concentration and the activation threshold change.
A reporter stays quiet across low densities, rises abruptly, and then remains high after modest dilution; interpret thresholding and possible positive feedback in the communication circuit.

train.scenario_anchor: One microbial strain cannot synthesize an essential vitamin and grows only beside a strain that releases that vitamin; request how metabolite exchange, auxotrophy, and partner dependence sustain both populations.

The same two strains coexist when adjacent in a structured habitat but fail when separated by a long diffusion distance; contrast spatial gradients and access to exchanged metabolites without invoking density signals.

A stable mixed community must partition one primary resource while one partner consumes an inhibitory metabolic byproduct; ask about producer-consumer balance, exchange rates, partner burden, and stability tradeoffs.

Removing one low-abundance partner causes an exchanged intermediate to accumulate while another strain loses a required downstream product; diagnose the broken metabolic dependency and cascading community failure.

test.scenario_anchor: Two metabolically dependent strains are placed on opposite sides of a membrane that passes small metabolites but not cells; predict when exchange remains sufficient and how diffusion limits partner growth.

Isotope tracing shows carbon entering one strain and later appearing in a distinct metabolite inside its partner; interpret the evidence for directional cross-feeding and identify alternative non-signaling explanations to rule out.

train.scenario_anchor: A buried fault segment remains locked during slow regional loading and then slips abruptly; request how frictional locking, elastic strain, failure, and rebound produce sudden rupture.

A smooth fault patch slips repeatedly in small events while a rough neighboring patch remains locked much longer; contrast friction, stress accumulation, nucleation, and event size across the two patches.

A hazard model must represent both strong rupture barriers and weaker connections between adjacent fault segments; ask how barrier strength and segment coupling affect whether rupture stops or propagates.
A rupture slows at a material contrast, crosses it, and then accelerates along a neighboring fault patch; diagnose changes in available stress, frictional resistance, and rupture propagation.

test.scenario_anchor: Only one portion of a previously locked fault slips while the adjacent portion remains intact; predict how stress transfer changes near-term failure tendency on the unslipped portion and nearby faults.

Wave arrival patterns imply one-way rupture growth, while later small events migrate toward the rupture edge; interpret rupture direction, stress redistribution, and the aftershock pattern without naming a place.

train.scenario_anchor: A cut hillside begins moving after prolonged rainfall raises water pressure within the soil; request how gravity, pore pressure, effective strength, and a potential slip surface produce failure.
Two slopes share the same angle and soil, but one retains deep roots while the other has recently lost vegetation; contrast reinforcement, erosion, water entry, and resistance to downslope motion.

A road embankment needs a combination of drainage and mechanical reinforcement under limited maintenance capacity; ask about stability benefits, failure modes, and tradeoffs of drainage, retaining support, and slope geometry.
A thin weak layer beneath stronger material fails and produces unexpectedly long downslope runout; diagnose slip-surface formation, material weakening, acceleration, and runout controls.

test.scenario_anchor: Excavation removes supporting material from the toe of a previously stable slope without changing rainfall; predict changes in resisting forces, deformation, and failure likelihood.

Instruments show rising pore pressure at one depth and accelerating displacement along a narrow subsurface zone; interpret the likely slip surface and whether drainage or structural support addresses the mechanism.

train.scenario_anchor: A dissolved accidental spill forms an elongated plume along the direction of groundwater flow; request how advection, dispersion, sorption, and degradation determine plume movement and shape.

Two dissolved chemicals enter the same aquifer, but one advances rapidly while the other remains near the source; contrast mobility through sorption, degradation, and interactions with aquifer material.
A cleanup plan must place monitoring wells and choose remediation under strongly heterogeneous permeability; ask about source localization, plume coverage, missed pathways, and cleanup tradeoffs.

Pumping lowers dissolved concentrations quickly, but contamination rebounds after pumping stops; diagnose slow release from low-permeability zones, incomplete source removal, and transport limitations.

test.scenario_anchor: Natural degradation becomes faster while groundwater velocity and source input remain unchanged; predict changes in plume length, peak concentration, and persistence.

Concentrations rise first in one monitoring line, later in another, and remain elevated near a low-permeability lens; interpret flow direction, dispersion, heterogeneity, and possible source location.

train.scenario_anchor: A coastal aquifer maintains freshwater above denser seawater under steady natural recharge; request how density contrast and hydraulic gradients establish the freshwater-seawater interface.
A shallow well and a deep well pump at similar rates, but only the deep well develops rapidly rising salinity; contrast broad interface movement with localized upconing beneath the wells.

A water manager must allocate limited recharge and reduce extraction while maintaining a freshwater supply; ask about recharge placement, pumping distribution, interface stabilization, and monitoring tradeoffs.
Salinity remains elevated long after a heavily pumped well is shut down; diagnose slow hydraulic recovery, residual saltwater geometry, and why stopping extraction is not immediately restorative.

test.scenario_anchor: Temporary seawater inundation raises salinity at the aquifer surface while groundwater extraction stays unchanged; predict density-driven movement, flushing, and which aquifer depths recover first.
Vertical salinity profiles rise sharply near one deep well but shift gradually across a wider coastal transect; interpret evidence for localized upconing versus regional landward interface movement.

train.scenario_anchor: The same community appears to change composition after an enumeration replaces several identity categories with broader ones; request how administrative classification and record revision can create apparent demographic change.

Settled households are counted consistently while seasonal workers and temporary lodgers are often missed; contrast enumeration access, residence rules, household definitions, and undercount mechanisms.

An enumeration form must balance continuity with earlier categories against allowing residents to describe identities not represented before; ask about comparability, state legibility, imposed categories, self-identification, and revision tradeoffs.

Residents sharing crowded dwellings are recorded as one household, causing some individuals to vanish from official totals; diagnose how household rules, enumerator practice, and local conditions create omission.

test.scenario_anchor: An enumeration changes from usual residence to location on the counting day for people living in collective housing; predict effects on household composition, local counts, and longitudinal comparability.

Age and occupation totals shift abruptly at the same time category labels and coding instructions change; interpret whether the discontinuity reflects population change, classification revision, or enumeration practice.

train.scenario_anchor: Two neighboring parcel records disagree after the physical landmark used in an older boundary description disappears; request how surveys, maps, deeds, and boundary evidence are reconciled in a parcel dispute.

One landholding follows customary shared-use rights while an adjacent holding has a formal individual title; contrast how each tenure form is represented, transferred, disputed, and brought into a cadastral record.

A land-tax system must choose valuation frequency and evidence requirements for parcels with uneven improvements; ask about assessment accuracy, administrative cost, appeal safeguards, and equitable valuation.

A parcel was divided informally, but the ledger still treats it as one holding and issues conflicting tax claims; diagnose how delayed survey and title updates create double assessment and boundary disputes.

test.scenario_anchor: A shared access route is omitted when several informal holdings are converted into registered parcels; predict effects on use rights, parcel value, disputes, and corrective record procedures.
Successive maps show parcel subdivisions that appear in the tax ledger only after long delays; interpret the sequence of surveying, registration, valuation, and administrative control.

train.scenario_anchor: A cargo vessel is detained because disease may emerge after arrival even when no crew member is visibly ill; request how incubation uncertainty, inspection, detention, and cargo rules reduce transmission while disrupting trade.

Officials consider isolating exposed households or placing a temporary cordon around the entire affected settlement; contrast transmission control, compliance, enforcement burden, relief needs, and collateral disruption.
A temporary quarantine station has limited inspection, lodging, food, and medical capacity; ask how detention length, surveillance, humane support, and release criteria should be balanced.

Potentially infectious goods bypass inspection through an informal unloading route and seed new cases inland; diagnose the enforcement gap, goods-control failure, and surveillance response without making identity documents central.

test.scenario_anchor: A faster diagnostic test becomes available while the disease incubation period remains uncertain; predict effects on detention duration, false release risk, capacity, and compliance.
Case counts fall inside a cordon while evasion reports and shortages rise near its boundary; interpret epidemiological effectiveness alongside enforcement, relief, and legitimacy problems.

train.scenario_anchor: A traveler reaches a border with a document whose identity claim and entry eligibility must be verified; request how credentials, records, inspection, and administrative decisions control admission and residence.

A government uses visas at external borders but travel permits for movement between internal regions; contrast legal authority, identity checks, eligibility rules, policing, and exclusion in the two systems.

Several generic jurisdictions need interoperable travel documents while retaining different admission rules; ask about verification, privacy, fraud resistance, revocation, and administrative discretion tradeoffs.

Conflicting birth and citizenship records cause repeated denial of a resident's travel document and no clear appeal path; diagnose record linkage, status determination, discretion, exclusion, and procedural safeguards.

test.scenario_anchor: A sudden displacement leaves many applicants without complete identity documents while ordinary admission rules remain in force; predict how temporary credentials, verification standards, residency decisions, and fairness pressures may change.

Approval records show similar applications receiving different outcomes across offices and applicant categories; interpret the role of administrative discretion, classification, policing priorities, and appeal mechanisms.

train.scenario_anchor: A document assistant encounters the word seal in passages about both closing containers and marine animals; request how surrounding words, topic, and selectional constraints identify the intended word sense.

The same adjective receives a literal physical reading in one sentence and a figurative evaluation in another; contrast contextual evidence for related polysemous senses without discussing competing parse attachments.

A search system must group related senses enough to recover useful documents without merging unrelated homonyms; ask about sense inventories, context representation, recall, precision, and granularity tradeoffs.

A clinical note tool interprets a common word by its everyday sense rather than its specialized medical sense; diagnose domain-sensitive word-sense disambiguation failure and the contextual cues that were ignored.

test.scenario_anchor: A familiar word acquires a new technical sense in a previously unseen domain while retaining its ordinary senses; predict how sparse domain context affects sense selection and what evidence could support adaptation.

Readers slow down after an ambiguous noun only when the following verb is incompatible with its initially preferred sense; interpret contextual reanalysis, sense preference, and whether the senses behave like homonymy or polysemy.

train.scenario_anchor: A prepositional phrase follows a verb and a noun, and either element can grammatically host the modifier; request how competing attachments create two structural interpretations and how context favors one.

A relative clause after two nouns attaches to the nearer noun in one context and the more distant noun in another; contrast structural, semantic, and locality cues while keeping individual word senses fixed.

A technical-writing guide must reduce modifier ambiguity without making every sentence unnaturally repetitive; ask about reordering, punctuation, explicit relative clauses, and clarity-style tradeoffs.
A parser attaches a location phrase to an action rather than the object being selected, causing an incorrect procedure; diagnose the competing parse structures and the missing attachment cues.

test.scenario_anchor: A spoken instruction gains a pause before its final modifier while all words remain unchanged; predict how prosody shifts attachment preference and the resulting sentence interpretation.
Reading time rises at a late phrase that forces a modifier to attach differently from the reader's initial parse; interpret structural reanalysis and evidence for competing attachment preferences.

train.scenario_anchor: In rapid speech, a word-final consonant shifts its place of articulation toward the following consonant; request how neighboring articulation produces regressive place assimilation and affects intelligibility.
A consonant keeps its underlying voicing in careful speech but adopts a neighbor's voicing in fast speech; contrast rate, direction, categorical rules, and gradient phonetic realization.
A speech synthesizer must add realistic coarticulation without making adjacent segments difficult to distinguish; ask about naturalness, clarity, context sensitivity, and gradient-control tradeoffs.

A transcription system consistently misses vowel nasalization before nasal consonants and treats each vowel as context-free; diagnose anticipatory assimilation and the acoustic evidence the system ignores.

test.scenario_anchor: A sound sequence changes so the influencing consonant comes before rather than after the target sound; predict how progressive versus regressive influence changes the location and direction of assimilation.

Acoustic measurements form a continuum across speaking rates, but listeners report a sharp category boundary; interpret gradient coarticulation, categorical perception, and evidence for rule-like versus continuous assimilation.

train.scenario_anchor: A speaker produces an adjective with gender marking that conflicts with the noun controlling it; request how controller and target features are represented and why a mismatch is ungrammatical.

Subject-verb number agreement is reliable when adjacent but attracts errors when an intervening noun has the opposite number; contrast locality, feature attraction, and long-distance controller-target dependencies.
Teaching material must explain case agreement in a language where word order can vary widely; ask how grammatical roles, visible morphology, distance, and example complexity should be balanced.

A copied narrative changes a pronoun's person and number after a long intervening clause, breaking agreement with its controller; diagnose feature transmission, distance effects, and the resulting morphological mismatch.

test.scenario_anchor: The grammatical person of a coordinated subject changes while number and sentence structure remain fixed; predict the target verb form and explain how person-resolution rules determine agreement.

Agreement errors rise with controller-target distance and are highest when an intervening noun carries conflicting features; interpret locality, attraction, and feature-matching mechanisms without discussing speech-sound influence.

train.scenario_anchor: A temperature regulator overshoots its setpoint and oscillates after a sudden external disturbance; request how error feedback, loop gain, delay, and damping produce overshoot and settling.

Two motor-speed loops use the same measured output, but one has low gain and responds slowly while the other has high gain and rings; contrast response speed, disturbance rejection, overshoot, and stability margins.
A liquid-level controller must reject inflow disturbances without commanding abrupt valve motion; ask about tuning, settling time, actuator wear, measurement noise, and robustness tradeoffs.

A controller keeps integrating error while its actuator is saturated, then produces a large overshoot when the actuator recovers; diagnose saturation, integral windup, instability risk, and anti-windup safeguards.

test.scenario_anchor: A fixed sensing delay is added to a previously stable position-control loop without changing its gain; predict changes in phase lag, overshoot, oscillation, and stability.

A step response rises quickly, overshoots repeatedly, and settles only after several diminishing oscillations; interpret loop damping and tuning from the response while keeping latent-state inference out of scope.

train.scenario_anchor: A moving platform must infer position and velocity from noisy sensors and an imperfect motion model; request how prediction, measurement updates, and uncertainty combine into a latent-state estimate.

One sensor becomes much noisier while a second sensor and the dynamical model remain unchanged; contrast measurement weighting, covariance, and estimate confidence before and after the noise increase.

A monitoring system must choose a small sensor set that makes all important internal states observable; ask about observability, redundancy, uncertainty, cost, and model-dependence tradeoffs without requesting control actions.

State estimates drift in one direction because the prediction model omits a persistent disturbance; diagnose model mismatch, biased innovations, covariance consistency, and possible estimator augmentation.

test.scenario_anchor: All measurements disappear for a short interval while the prediction model continues to run; predict how estimate uncertainty and error evolve before measurements resume.
Innovation residuals remain biased and reported covariance stays small despite growing disagreement with later observations; interpret model mismatch and overconfidence in the estimator.

train.scenario_anchor: A rotating shaft develops a small surface crack after many load reversals even though no single load is extreme; request how cyclic stress initiates a crack and drives propagation per cycle.
A smooth specimen and a notched specimen experience the same cyclic load, but the notched one cracks much earlier; contrast stress concentration, crack nucleation, and early growth.

A maintenance plan must choose inspection intervals for a component with measurable crack growth under repeated loading; ask about detection limits, growth rate, load spectrum, safety margin, and downtime tradeoffs.
A component fails sooner under occasional overload cycles mixed into an otherwise moderate cyclic history; diagnose how variable amplitude and crack-tip effects alter initiation and propagation.

test.scenario_anchor: The cyclic load amplitude is reduced while material, geometry, and cycle frequency stay fixed; predict changes in crack initiation time, growth per cycle, and service life.

Inspection data show a long period with no visible crack followed by steadily accelerating crack length across later cycles; interpret initiation, detectable growth, stress intensity, and approach to fracture.

train.scenario_anchor: A polymer beam under an unchanging load develops slow permanent sag even though the load never cycles; request how sustained stress produces time-dependent strain and eventual loss of shape.
Identical alloy samples carry the same constant stress, but the hotter sample deforms much faster; contrast temperature-dependent creep rate, microstructural mechanisms, and rupture time.
A high-temperature support must balance allowable sustained stress against required service duration; ask about material choice, steady creep rate, safety margin, inspection, and lifetime tradeoffs.
A heated bolted joint gradually loses preload despite an unchanged external load; diagnose creep or stress relaxation in the joint materials and the resulting loss of clamping force.

test.scenario_anchor: The grain structure of a hot loaded component is changed while sustained stress and temperature stay fixed; predict how microstructural deformation mechanisms, creep rate, and lifetime may change.

A strain-time record under constant load first slows, then becomes nearly linear, and finally accelerates toward rupture; interpret primary, secondary, and tertiary creep and what the transition says about damage.
